prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1067; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a sideswipe while changing lanes and described a sharp neck jolt along with immediate stiffness. Photos taken at the scene show damage consistent with the described impact, and the vehicle's damage pattern matches the account given.

Entry 2: A review of the policy confirms the driver is named on it and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle was damaged before coverage began, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known.

Entry 3: The police report and statements from the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the scene photos are the main independent record of the event.

Entry 4: The claimant was contacted by phone and gave the same account of the collision as in the initial report. Details of the lane change and the point of contact did not shift between conversations.

Entry 5: Medical records show whiplash diagnosed shortly after the collision, which fits the kind and force of the crash. No earlier injury to the same area of the neck or upper back is known from the claimant's history or prior claims search.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course of physiotherapy and medication, and the reported symptoms eased steadily as the patient improved. Records from the most recent visit show the treatment has tapered off.

Entry 7: Based on the photos, the damage, the police confirmation, the consistent account, and the medical course, the file supports the claim as presented. Next step is to finalize the injury settlement review with the treating provider's final report.
